chunks: If the (enemy) had entered the city from every side and asked them to rise in revolt, they would have done so, and not hesitated but a little;

key_terms.أَقْطَارِهَا: sides, quarters, or directions (referring to the city/fortress)
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةَ: revolt, rebellion, or trial (specifically rebellion against the Muslims)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the hesitation of Banu Qurayza before rebelling?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the innate disposition (fitrah) of the Banu Qurayza, illustrating that their potential for treachery was not merely situational but inherent. In Shia exegesis, this is often viewed as a sign of their hypocrisy (munafiqun), where outward allegiance masked an immediate readiness to switch sides for political gain. The brevity of their hesitation underscores the depth of their insincerity in the covenant with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
